# Research notes: Romans 8, verse by verse

**Gaps:** I didn't find Lutheran (lcms.org, 1517.org), Orthodox (oca.org), modern scholarship (netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org), or prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace material on this chapter. I also found no Pentecostal teacher defending the "tongues" reading of v. 26; I only found critics of it. Enduring Word's full text cut off after vv. 12–13, so my notes on Guzik's later verses come from the page summary. Treat this as a first pass.

**Sources used:**
- Guzik (Enduring Word): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Wesley's Notes: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- Matthew Henry: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley's sermons: https://ccel.org/ccel/wesley/sermons.all.html

---

**v. 1**
- Guzik says the verdict isn't "less condemnation." Believers' standing has been completely changed, not just improved. The verdict is not "less condemnation" but a complete transformation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Guzik and Spurgeon: the closing words "who do not walk according to the flesh…" (in the KJV/NKJV) are not found in the earliest ancient manuscripts of Romans. They were probably copied in from v. 4. Walking by the Spirit is not a *condition* for their status of no condemnation. https://enduringword.com/no-condemnation/
- Henry: believers may still be disciplined, but they are not condemned. They may be chastened of the Lord, but not condemned with the world. Now this arises from their being in Christ Jesus. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- **Where traditions differ (Methodist):** Wesley's notes say "no condemnation" covers things present or past. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm His sermon on this verse attaches a condition: there is no condemnation so long as they do not yield thereto… so long as they maintain a continual war with all sin. He adds that they are not condemned… for sins of infirmity. https://ccel.org/ccel/wesley/sermons.all.html

**v. 2**
- Guzik: v. 1 frees us from sin's guilt, v. 2 from its power. Romans 8:1 tells us we are free from the *guilt* of sin. Romans 8:2 tells us we are free from the *power* of sin. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Henry reads it the same way: freedom both from the guilt and power of sin. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley gives a different reading of the terms: The law of the Spirit - That is, the gospel. Hath freed me from the law of sin and death - That is, the Mosaic dispensation. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 3**
- Guzik: the law can expose sin but cannot beat it. Christ came "in the likeness of sinful flesh," meaning truly human but without sin. Jesus was not sinful flesh, but He identified with it entirely. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Henry: the fault was not in the law itself but *through the flesh,* through the corruption of human nature. Sin still lives in believers, but only like that of a condemned malefactor. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley: God gave sentence, that sin should be destroyed, and the believer wholly delivered from it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 4**
- Guzik stresses that the law is fulfilled "in us," not "by us." Christ is our substitute for both obedience and punishment. It isn't fulfilled *by* us, but **in us**. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- **Where traditions differ (Methodist):** Wesley takes "righteousness of the law" to mean the holiness it required, actually worked out in those guided in all our thoughts, words, and actions, not by corrupt nature, but by the Spirit of God. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**vv. 5–8**
- Guzik: where your mind is set shows whether you walk by the flesh or the Spirit. "Flesh" means sinful rebellion, not normal bodily needs. Paul means only the sinful gratification of those needs. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Guzik on v. 8: In the flesh we cannot please God, even if the flesh does religious things that are admired by men. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Henry on v. 7: the carnal mind isn't just distant from God; it actively opposes Him. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley on v. 6: the carnal mind is The sure mark of spiritual death, and the way to death everlasting. The spiritual mind brings peace with God, the opposite of the "enmity" in v. 7. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 9**
- Guzik: every believer has the Spirit. He calls it a misnomer to split Christians into "Spirit-filled" and "non-Spirit-filled," though many still miss the ongoing filling commanded in Ephesians 5:18. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Wesley: anyone without the Spirit is not a Christian; not in a state of salvation. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-romans/

**v. 10**
- Henry: the body is still mortal and sentenced to die, but the spirit is now spiritually alive. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley agrees the body is dead - Devoted to death. Because of sin - Heretofore committed. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- Guzik reads "body" differently, as the old man, which had to die when Christ came in. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/

**v. 11**
- Guzik: the Spirit will carry salvation through to our mortal bodies by resurrection. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/ (Wesley's notes have no comment on this verse.)

**vv. 12–13**
- Guzik: living by the flesh always ends in death. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Henry: "you will die" means eternal death. Putting sin to death is a joint work. we cannot do it without the Spirit working it in us, and the Spirit will not do it without our doing our endeavour. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley: the deeds to kill include Not only evil actions, but evil desires, tempers, thoughts. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/romans-8.html

**v. 14**
- Guzik: being led by the Spirit is the real mark of God's children, not church attendance or other outward habits. It is not a precondition for sonship: we become sons first and then the Spirit of God leads us. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/

**v. 15**
- Guzik: adoption means a close, joyful relationship with God instead of the bondage and fear of the law. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Wesley: using both "Abba" and "Father" may point to Jewish and Gentile believers crying out together. The "spirit of bondage" is the same Holy Spirit convicting a sinner at first, before He works as the Spirit of adoption. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- Henry: it is God's prerogative, when he adopts, to give a spirit of adoption-the nature of children. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- **Catholic/Orthodox shared heritage (Chrysostom):** he admits the "spirit of bondage" is very perplexing. He compares the Spirit of adoption to the Spirit of prophecy: the believer calls God Father as moved by the Spirit. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/chrysostom/romans/8.htm

**v. 16**
- **Distinctively Methodist:** Wesley holds that the Spirit gives a testimony distinct from that of his own spirit, or the testimony of a good conscience. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm In his sermons he argues this direct witness comes before our own awareness of being holy. He also says that denying it does in effect deny justification by faith. https://ccel.org/ccel/wesley/sermons.all.html

**v. 17**
- Wesley: "if we suffer with Him" means suffering Willingly and cheerfully, for righteousness' sake. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- Chrysostom: the promise is not land, as in Israel's case, but a share in the inheritance with the Only-Begotten Son, wholly spiritual. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/chrysostom/romans/8.htm

**v. 18**
- Henry: suffering cannot earn that glory, and, if suffering for Christ will not merit, much less will doing. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm

**vv. 19–22**
- Guzik: creation was subjected to futility on account of man's sin, and will benefit from the ultimate redemption of men. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Wesley: "creation" means all visible creatures, believers excepted. The one who subjected it was God (Gen. 3:17). On v. 21 he argues Destruction is not deliverance, so creation will be restored, not destroyed. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm He develops this in his sermon "The General Deliverance" on vv. 19–22. https://ccel.org/ccel/wesley/sermons.all.html
- A Seedbed writer warns that this promise of creation set free gets misconstrued because it is severed from the larger biblical story of God's plan for the whole earth. https://seedbed.com/misplacing-romans-john-wesley-and-hermeneutics/

**vv. 23–25**
- Guzik: we are already adopted (v. 15), but we still wait for that adoption to be completed when our bodies are redeemed. https://es.enduringword.com/comentario-biblico/romanos-8/
- Wesley: Romans would publicly acknowledge someone already adopted in private. In the same way, God will publicly own His children at the resurrection. On v. 24: We do not yet possess this full salvation. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**vv. 26–27**
- Henry: Christ intercedes for us in heaven, the Spirit intercedes for us in our hearts. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley: the groanings come from us, but the Spirit forms them. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- Barnes disagrees: the verse does not mean that the Spirit produces these groanings; rather, He helps and sustains us in them. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/romans/8-26.html
- **Pentecostal/charismatic debate:** some take the "groans" as praying in tongues. Precept Austin quotes Ryrie and others rejecting this: This is not the gift of tongues, for these groans are not in words. https://www.preceptaustin.org/romans_826-27 I found no Pentecostal source making the case for the tongues reading.

**v. 28**
- Wesley: "all things" means Ease or pain, poverty or riches, working for spiritual and eternal good. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- A Bible.org lesson argues the verse only works if God has an eternal purpose that He is able to accomplish in spite of sinful people and their so-called "free will." https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-51-all-things-good-us-romans-828

**vv. 29–30 (the main dividing point)**
- **Reformed (Ligonier):** the "golden chain" is the inviolable order in which our Creator saves His people. Salvation is God's work from start to finish. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/golden-chain-salvation
- **Reformed (Sinclair Ferguson):** the four links are aspects of union with Christ, so it's the Lord Jesus Christ Himself who is the gold. https://learn.ligonier.org/podcasts/things-unseen-with-sinclair-ferguson/a-golden-chain-or-is-it
- **Reformed (TGC):** a former Arminian says the chain explains how we can "know" v. 28. It is very much about a guarantee. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/romans-8-made-calvinist/
- **Reformed (Henry):** "called" means the internal and effectual call. "Glorified" is in the past tense because of the certainty of it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- **Evangelical (GotQuestions):** the call in v. 30 is the effectual call. https://www.gotquestions.org/golden-chain-of-salvation.html
- **Methodist/Wesleyan (Wesley):** the people foreknown are those who are conformable to the image of his Son. Those justified are glorified only if they continue in God's goodness (Rom. 11:22). Paul does not deny that a believer may fall away; he only affirms that this is the method whereby God leads us step by step toward heaven. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm
- **Methodist/Wesleyan (Wesley's sermon "On Predestination"):** God's fixed decree is that believers will be saved. Those He foreknows as believers, He calls both outwardly and inwardly. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/the-sermons-of-john-wesley-1872-edition/sermon-58-on-predestination/
- **Methodist/Wesleyan (Arminian Magazine):** reading the chain as unbreakable dates from Beza and Perkins. Wesley's teaching on prevenient grace broke "the chain of logical necessity". https://wesley.nnu.edu/arminianism/the-arminian-magazine/issue-1-spring-2002-volume-20/
- **Catholic (Jimmy Akin, catholic.com):** he sums up the Calvinist claims as unconditional choice, predestination to final salvation, and certain glorification, then says all of these claims are false. The snippet I saw didn't include his reasons. https://www.catholic.com/audio/tjap/what-is-the-golden-chain-of-salvation

**v. 31**
- Henry: God is for them, even when he seems to act against them. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Guzik: the "if" is a guard. God is for us only if we are reconciled to Him through Christ. https://es.enduringword.com/comentario-biblico/romanos-8/

**v. 32**
- **Where traditions differ:** Henry reads "for us all" as for all the elect and as substitution, in our place. He argues that the One who prepared a kingdom for us will supply what we need on the way. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rom/Rom_008.cfm
- Wesley: "all things" means things Needful or profitable for us. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 33**
- **Where traditions differ (Methodist):** Wesley reads "elect" through Israel's history. In the Old Testament the term covered the whole visible nation. In the New Testament it applies to members of the invisible church, and nothing could cut them off from these but their own wilful apostasy. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 34**
- Wesley: faith should not stop at Christ's death but take in His resurrection, reign and return. He intercedes by presenting his obedience, his sufferings, his prayers, and our prayers sanctified through him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 35**
- Wesley: Paul lists troubles from lesser to greater. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/romans/8.htm

**v. 37**
- Guzik: we are "more than conquerors" because we lose nothing even in battle. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/romans-8/
- Wesley's sermon: the person under grace fights and conquers, yea, is "more than conqueror". https://ccel.org/ccel/wesley/sermons.all.html

**vv. 38–39**
- Wesley: "present" and "future" cover all times; "height" and "depth" cover all places. Height stands for heaven, depth for the abyss. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/romans-8.html
- Chrysostom calls this a bond of Christ's love that not even angels can loosen. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/230108.htm

**Nothing found:** v. 36.
